questions.text: Which use of AI in summarisation does the lesson call the pedagogically stronger one?

options.text: Asking AI to produce the summary first, so the student has a correct model to study from.
Writing the summary yourself, then asking AI to compare it with the original and say what you missed or misunderstood.
Asking AI to summarise the same text twice and comparing the two versions.
Asking AI to shorten the student's summary so that it is easier to revise from.

questions.explanation: When AI generates the summary the student holds a useful reference but has done none of the cognitive work; when AI evaluates the student's own summary, the student discovers their own gaps, which the lesson calls a far more powerful learning experience.

questions.text: The lesson mentions one tool that can turn generated flashcards into something a student can use straight away. What does it describe?

options.text: Claude's Artifacts feature can produce a working flashcard web application with a card-flipping interface, usable directly in the browser.
ChatGPT exports flashcard sets directly into spaced-repetition software.
The AI produces a print-ready PDF of cards for the student to cut out.
The AI schedules review reminders in the student's calendar.

questions.explanation: The lesson names Artifacts as an example of AI going beyond a list of cards: it generates an interactive flashcard application the student can practise with immediately, removing the need for a separate flashcard tool.

questions.text: Which classroom activities does the lesson suggest for helping students structure what they have learned?

options.text: At the end of a lesson, students write a five-sentence summary and then use AI to identify what they missed.
Before a test, students build their own flashcard set and then ask AI for additional cards covering blind spots.
After a complex text, students create their own outline, then compare it with an AI-generated one and discuss the differences.
The teacher distributes AI-generated notes so that the whole class works from one accurate record instead of taking their own notes.
Each topic is summarised once at the start of the year and that summary is kept unchanged as the definitive record.

questions.explanation: All three suggested activities put the student's own work first and use AI as a check. The lesson rejects replacing students' note-taking with someone else's notes, and describes knowledge structuring as a recurring cycle rather than a document written once.

questions.text: An AI-generated outline or comparison table is most useful when the student treats it as the finished organisation of the material and memorises it as it stands.
questions.explanation: The lesson advises treating AI-generated structures as starting points: students should review them, disagree where appropriate, rearrange elements and add their own connections and examples, because the goal is to build the student's own mental model.
